notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached and no real MuJoCo, ROS or hardware run is claimed. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card is family ros with helper RosDriver, but recon found no ROS service or action for stepping, resetting or stopping the simulated world. humanoid_mujoco_sim is a ROS 2 node whose only interfaces are Float32MultiArray target subscriptions and joint/odometry/IMU publications (humanoid_sim.py:45-55); its physics is a MuJoCo model stepped with mj.mj_step (humanoid_sim.py:127-131), and the card's models[0] is that MJCF. The card's hint capabilities are cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 and its mock_strategy is upstream-sim, so this package serves the pinned model through MujocoDriver (cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1) rather than pretending the ROS topic surface is a world step or inventing a stop service. The fact table cites only the topic declarations at humanoid_sim.py:45-55; the absence of a step, reset or stop service is recon evidence from a repository-wide search, not a line-level Fact. The model file is read in place from the read-only clone at cfb27eb205d6ee21a801abe273ffc0a53d3be0f2 and is never copied, imported or modified. The served model has a freejoint base and twelve hinge joints, so the world state has 19 qpos and 18 qvel values (humanoid_legged_control_.xml:70-164); the twelve motor actuators declare ctrllimited=true with per-joint ctrlranges of -150/150, -200/200 or -90/90 (lines 179-192), and the bridge derives the cap.world.step.v1 ctrl envelope from that model range, refusing out-of-range values before writing data.ctrl. The served step is the MJCF's own 0.001 s (line 4). cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData and mj_forward and restores the model defaults; the model's home keyframe (qpos z=1.5, lines 233-239) is not applied, and the upstream node's own override to qpos z=0.82 and twelve init joint angles (humanoid_sim.py:17-18,56-60) is disclosed in the fidelity gaps. A reset seed is accepted for the class contract but MuJoCo does not use it; cap.world.seed.v1 is intentionally not declared because this model path has no RNG seed control (determinism none), so an accepted-seed action would be a false determinism claim. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed here (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is the package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py, declared as the class FakeMujoco. The stand-in parses the same MJCF for the free joint, twelve hinges, twelve motors, their explicit ctrlranges and the 0.001 s step, but its integration is a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value; it loads no STL mesh, resolves no contact, inertia, gravity, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics, and does not implement mj_getState/mj_setState (the bridge uses its basic checkpoint profile). The fidelity gaps list these differences, the missing wall-clock pacing and GUI, and the unused ROS topics/controller nodes; no trajectory was compared with the real engine. The declared F1 describes the pinned MuJoCo model under the real engine; the deployed fake is a kinematic placeholder (no contacts or dynamics) and its limits are listed in the gaps. The real mujoco path (a backend that backends does not list) was not run. WARNINGS kept from the last gate run, all expected for a simulator-family stand-in (none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library rather than an upstream class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds eight cases (model shape from the card model, per-actuator control-range refusal with zero effect, control-vector length, step advancing integration state and time, reset to the model defaults, reset seed recorded without changing the model, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); all pass. NOT COVERED: the ROS 2 target/state topics, /pauseFlag publication and the controller nodes are not part of this driver; no real MuJoCo engine run, rosbridge/ROS graph, hardware or live deployment validation was performed. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. No site-limits.example.json is needed because no operator-required bound and no driver-declared Limit are present; the control envelope is derived from the pinned model at run time. The clone was read in place and remained unmodified.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the MujocoDriver deviation (the repository has no ROS service or action; HumanoidSim's node only publishes state topics and /pauseFlag and subscribes to target topics, humanoid_sim.py:45-55, while the card's only model is the MJCF that it steps with mj_step, 127-131), all 14 facts, the twelve ctrlranges the bridge derives its envelope from (humanoid_legged_control_.xml:179-192), the stand-in mujoco module and the lockstep software latch, which does stop this simulation from advancing. Five facts said more than their lines (a 'so' inference on the freejoint, MuJoCoBase and main named off their ranges with main called a HumanoidSim method although it is a module function at 279, the start-state fact omitting the qpos[3:7] write, the node fact omitting /pauseFlag, and an 'at most 1/60 s' loop bound that the <= condition does not give), and the fake backend was published with the real engine's F1 'mujoco' fidelity contract, which a test asserted, although it is a kinematic placeholder with no physics. Reviewer changed driver.py (the five facts narrowed or widened to their lines; fidelity keeps F1 for the real-engine backend and fidelity_by_backend['fake'] publishes the stand-in as F0, as pocketxjl/humanoid-control does, with the gaps split into shared and fake-only lists), test_driver.py (the fidelity case expects the F0 stand-in contract) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected MuJoCo-family warnings (G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, G8.NO_UNIT x3) and the digest unchanged. RESULT.json notes written before the fix are superseded where they say the declared F1 contract covers the deployed fake and that the fidelity case checks it: the fake now publishes the F0 stand-in contract (coordinator pattern 7). For the human reviewer: The package serves the bare MuJoCo plant: raw ctrl torques on twelve leg motors with no OCS2/WBC controller, so the humanoid falls unless a caller supplies the controller's torques; reset restores the MJCF defaults (base at z 0, all joints 0), not the upstream start pose (z 0.82, bent knees) or the home keyframe. The lockstep latch stops stepping. No hardware path exists in the repository.
